details:
TLDR: I think removing the ability for users to manually show avatars outside of an instance performance gate is an unnecessary restriction of user choice and I would like to make the case for an alternative approach.

Hey everyone,

I would like to voice my disappointment about one aspect of the "Avatar Performance Gated Group Instances".

Let me first of all state that I fully understand the reasons behind why this is implemented. Defining an avatar rating for a group event has been standard practice in a lot of community events and providing a tool to make that better is something I support.

Yet the current implementation of it too heavily restricts an individuals user choice for, what is in my opinion, no benefit. Let me explain:

VRChat offers many features that allow a user to configure what Avatars they want to see or block. I personally block all Very Poor avatars by default, as to not be surprised by bad performance, but I also liberally use the Show Avatar feature to be make sure I can see the avatars of people I'm talking to. This is my choice and everyone is empowered by VRChat to make other choices, depending on their individual performance needs and hardware they have.

Now with Performance Gated instances specifically the ability to override and explicitly show someone's avatar is removed. And that particular part of the system I can't get behind at all. In my eyes that's an unnecessary removal of user freedom/choice and should be reverted.

I see this as part of a common pattern in many modern software products, where user choice is restricted in the believe that it will improve the overall experience. The end of the road for that are a lot of the problems we have with many modern software products, where choices are made for the user in many areas, which annoy a lot of people.

So here is what I propose instead:

Most aspects of the current implementation can stay the same. During instance creation a decision can be made as to which avatar rating should be recommended for the instance. During joining the instance, the popup regarding the performance of the current avatar can stay, but the part about "regardless of their avatar visibility settings" should be removed. On joining the instance, the client will enforce the default blocking behavior to not load avatars beyond the restriction. BUT crucially, a user SHOULD remain able to manually load an avatar with "Show avatar". This way a default can be given, which should improve the overall experience of players that never touch any of the settings. It also still incentivizes people to switch into a different avatar, as they are made aware of the fact that they will not be seen by most people. But if they are okay with that, they can use whatever they want and others can decide to see them, or not. User Choice is preserved, everyone wins.

Ofc I have to address the particular phrasing you have used here: "This is to prevent the slightly awkward dynamic of players asking others to show their avatar, thus defeating the point of the feature."

I have personally never encountered this, but I'm sure it can happen. Yet I don't think this is a sufficient justification to subvert the option of user choice. If a random person were to come up to me and ask me to enable their avatar, all they'd get from me is to get blocked, as that's just annoying behavior. For my friends, I chose on a case-by-case basis. I don't see how this defeats the point of the feature, as I have outlined before in my proposal.

I hope you will consider this feedback.
title: Allow overwriting instance-level avatar restrictions locally
